JenticCredentialId.description:
ID of the stored credential the broker resolved and used to sign
this execution. Present only when a stored credential was actually
used — a missing header unambiguously means no credential (inline
auth, a credential-less API, or a failure before resolution).

JenticCredentialName.description:
Human-readable label of the credential in `Jentic-Credential-Id`,
sanitized to printable ASCII (unsafe characters replaced with `?`).
Present under the same condition as the id header. The same header
name is also accepted on requests to disambiguate credential
resolution.

JenticExecutionId.description: Execution ID — unique identifier for this brokered request.

ServerTiming.description:
W3C Server-Timing. When the upstream sends its own
`Server-Timing`, it is forwarded. When the deployment
enables `broker.server_timing` (off by default), the Broker
appends a second field with per-stage durations in milliseconds
for authenticated callers: `jentic-auth`, `jentic-egress`,
`jentic-discover`, `jentic-rules`, `jentic-body`,
`jentic-idempotency`, `jentic-cred`, `jentic-upstream`,
`jentic-persist`, `jentic-total` — fixed names in the reserved
`jentic-` namespace (an upstream entry claiming that prefix is
dropped), no identifiers. Only the stages that ran are listed. On
a streamed response the headers precede the body, so
`jentic-upstream` is the wait for the upstream headers and
`jentic-persist` is absent. The field also appears on
post-authentication error responses: with durations once the
upstream was called (e.g. a `504`), and as stage names only for an
error the Broker raises before the upstream call (e.g. `404`,
`403`, `409`, `424`). `jentic-upstream` includes the circuit-breaker
check, so a circuit-open `503` carries durations even though no
upstream request was sent. It never appears on `401`, a missing-permission
`403`, a rate-limit `429` or a load-shed `503`.

examples: jentic-auth;dur=1.4, jentic-egress;dur=0.3, jentic-discover;dur=0.9, jentic-rules;dur=2.1, jentic-body;dur=0.1, jentic-cred;dur=3.0, jentic-upstream;dur=84.2, jentic-persist;dur=4.7, jentic-total;dur=97.6

Traceparent.description:
W3C Trace Context — `00-{trace-id}-{parent-id}-01`. The
`parent-id` is the broker span; downstream services use this to
link their own spans into the same distributed trace. Version
`00` is current; flags `01` = sampled.

Tracestate.description:
W3C Trace Context vendor extensions. Jentic packs a fixed
five-field value under the `jentic` vendor key:
`jentic=<exec_id>:<toolkit_id>:<vendor>:<name>:<version>`, e.g.
`jentic=exec_xyz789:_:stripe:payments:2023-10-16`. The
first two segments answer *who is calling*; the trailing
segments answer *what is being called*. Missing segments are
emitted as `_` so the shape stays positionally parseable — the
second segment is a legacy slot (toolkit attribution on the
pre-theme-5 path, whose tables were dropped in Phase 6b) and is
always `_` on current executions. Composable with other vendors
(`jentic=...,datadog=...`).

IdempotencyKey.description:
Optional caller-supplied key to make this request idempotent.
If present, the broker dedupes against the key for 24 hours
and replays the original response on retry. UUIDv4 recommended.
See the `Idempotency` section above for full semantics.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

JenticCredentialId.description:
Disambiguate credential resolution by exact credential id — the
authoritative signal, applied before the name filter and
specificity narrowing. Ids are stable and non-secret
(`cred_`-prefixed); the `409 ambiguous_credential_binding`
candidate list carries them. An id that matches no covering,
bound candidate is rejected with `400 credential_id_not_found`
(candidates listed). Consumed by the broker — never forwarded
upstream. The same header name is also emitted on responses to
attribute the credential used.
JenticCredentialId.name: Jentic-Credential-Id

JenticCredentialName.description:
Disambiguate credential resolution by the credential's
human-readable name. When several bound credentials cover the
target API at the same specificity (a multi-account setup), the
broker refuses with `409 ambiguous_credential_binding` and lists
the candidates; resend with this header naming the one to use. A
name that matches no covering candidate is rejected with
`400 credential_name_not_found` (candidates listed). Consumed by
the broker — never forwarded upstream. The same header name is
also emitted on responses to attribute the credential used.
JenticCredentialName.name: Jentic-Credential-Name

JenticReason.description:
Why the agent is making this call, in its own words. Send it on
any call that changes something: when the call is held for human
approval, the reviewer sees it next to the request. Percent-encode
it as UTF-8 (a header carries ASCII only); at most 1024 characters
after decoding (longer text is cut, control characters other than
newline and tab are dropped). Consumed by the broker — never
forwarded upstream, and dropped when the call runs straight away.
JenticReason.name: Jentic-Reason

JenticRevision.description:
Pin upstream-API resolution to a specific `ApiRevision`
instead of the API's `current_revision_id`. Multi-valued —
repeat the header (or comma-separate) once per API you
want to pin. Each value is `vendor:name:version=<revision_id>`:
`vendor`, `name` and `version` are the API's `api` reference,
and `<revision_id>` is the revision's `revision_id` exactly as
the control plane returns it (`GET
/apis/{vendor}/{name}/{version}/revisions`, the revision get,
an import job's result, or `jentic apis revisions`). The
equivalent `rev_<revision_id without hyphens>` label is
accepted too.

Use cases:

- Test a `draft` revision against existing credentials
  before promoting it.
- Reproduce a historical execution against an `archived`
  spec for diagnostic purposes (refused by default;
  archived revisions are not pinnable from the hot path).

The Broker forwards the pin into the control-plane
`POST /lookup/operation` call so URL → `operation_id`
resolution sees the requested spec. When the header is
absent or the URL doesn't match a pinned API, the Broker
resolves against `current_revision_id` as today.

Pinning a `draft` revision the caller doesn't have
access to returns `403`. Pinning an unknown or
`archived` revision returns `422`. Pinning the same API
to two different revisions in one header returns
`422 invalid_revision_pin`; repeating the same revision
(in either form) is allowed. The chosen revisions
are recorded on the resulting `ExecutionRecord`
(`pinned_revisions` field on the control plane).
JenticRevision.name: Jentic-Revision

Prefer.description:
RFC 7240 processing preference. `wait={seconds}` — maximum time
to wait for a synchronous response before falling back to async.
`respond-async` — always queue and return `202` immediately.
Prefer.name: Prefer

UpstreamUrl.description: The URL of the upstream service to execute the request to.
UpstreamUrl.name: upstream_url

schema.description: The URL of the upstream service to execute the request to.
schema.title: Upstream Url

invalid_upstream_url.summary: Upstream URL rejected by the broker's egress policy.

value.detail: upstream URL resolves to a blocked address range
value.title: upstream URL resolves to a blocked address range

BadRequest.description:
Request rejected before reaching the upstream — malformed JSON,
missing required field, or schema-validation failure on the
broker side. Body is RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` using
the shared `ProblemDetails` schema.

ambiguous_credential_binding.summary: Two bound credentials cover the API; pick one with a header.

agent_directive.human_readable_instruction: Multiple bound credentials cover this API. Resend the same request with the Jentic-Credential-Id header set to one of the ids in parameters.candidates (Jentic-Credential-Name also works when names are unique).

value.detail: Ambiguous: 2 active credentials match api (api.github.com, main, 1.1.4)
value.title: Ambiguous: 2 active credentials match api (api.github.com, main, 1.1.4)

ambiguous_match.summary: The upstream URL matches several registered operations equally.

value.detail: Ambiguous URL match: 2 candidates with equal specificity
value.title: Ambiguous URL match: 2 candidates with equal specificity

idempotency_conflict.summary: Idempotency-Key reused with a different request.

value.detail: Idempotency-Key reused with a different request.
value.title: Idempotency-Key reused with a different request.

Conflict.description:
Conflict (RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`), distinguished by
the problem `type`:

- `ambiguous_credential_binding` — several credentials the caller
  is bound to cover the target API at the same specificity. The
  body lists the candidates (`id`, `name`, `last4`, `created_at`);
  resend with the `Jentic-Credential-Name` or `Jentic-Credential-Id`
  request header to pick one.
- `idempotency_conflict` — the same `Idempotency-Key` was already
  used with a different request (method, upstream URL, resolved
  credential, or body). Reusing a key for a different request is
  rejected; pick a new key.
- `idempotency_in_progress` — a request with this `Idempotency-Key`
  is still being processed. The response carries a `Retry-After`
  header; retry after that delay to obtain the replayed result.
- `ambiguous_match` — the upstream URL matches more than one
  registered operation with equal specificity, so the broker cannot
  tell which API the call is for. Raised before dispatch; the
  registered specs overlap and need an operator fix (or a
  `Jentic-Revision` pin that disambiguates).

credential_not_provisioned.summary: No credential connected for the API; ask a human to connect one.

agent_directive.human_readable_instruction: No credential is connected for 'api.example.com'; ask the user to connect the account before retrying.

value.detail: No credential provisioned for 'api.example.com'.
value.title: No credential provisioned for 'api.example.com'.

CredentialNotProvisioned.description:
A bound credential is an unusable dependency, so the broker cannot
sign the upstream call. Body is RFC 9457
`application/problem+json`; the `type` discriminates two cases with
opposite recovery paths:
- `credential_not_provisioned` — no credential is connected for the
  resolved upstream API. The `agent_directive` is a `prompt_human`
  instruction carrying an `intent_id` correlation id, so an
  autonomous agent stops and asks the user to connect the account
  rather than retrying or guessing the credential. When the agent
  already has an open connect session for the API, the directive
  also carries a non-secret `provisioning_url` — that session's
  owner approval link (`/app/agents?approve=<session_id>`) — for
  the agent to relay instead of starting another connect.
- `credential_undecryptable` — a credential is connected but its
  stored secret can no longer be decrypted (typically the
  deployment's encryption key rotated underneath it, e.g. a
  reinstall over existing data). The caller cannot self-provision
  and retrying will not help; the `prompt_human` directive tells
  the agent to ask an operator to remove and re-add the credential.

upstream_connect_failed.summary: The upstream refused the connection or its host did not resolve; no request bytes were sent, so a retry is safe for any method.

value.detail: The upstream connection could not be established.
value.title: The upstream connection could not be established.

upstream_connect_timeout.summary: Connecting to the upstream timed out; no request bytes were sent, so a retry is safe for any method.

value.detail: The upstream connection could not be established in time.
value.title: The upstream connection could not be established in time.

upstream_response_too_large.summary: The broker aborted an upstream response over its size cap.

value.detail: The upstream response exceeded the 10485760-byte response-size cap.
value.title: The upstream response exceeded the 10485760-byte response-size cap.

upstream_timeout.summary: Upstream did not respond within the broker's deadline.

value.detail: The upstream did not respond within the deadline.
value.title: The upstream did not respond within the deadline.

upstream_transport_error.summary: The upstream connection failed (e.g. dropped mid-response); 502 Bad Gateway. The request may have reached the upstream, so retry only an idempotent or Idempotency-Key'd call.

value.detail: Upstream transport error (RemoteProtocolError)
value.title: Upstream transport error (RemoteProtocolError)

Default.description:
Catch-all problem+json response for any status not enumerated on
this operation. Key recovery on the problem `type`, not the bare
status: one status can carry types with different retry safety
(a 502 `upstream_connect_failed` is safe to retry for any method;
a 502 `upstream_transport_error` may already have reached the
upstream), and one type can appear at more than one status
(`upstream_connect_failed` is 502 when the connection is refused
or the host does not resolve, 504 when connecting times out).

held.summary: Call held for human approval by a require-approval rule.

value.agent_directive: This call needs human approval. Most important: show the user the review_url, since they cannot approve it without that link, and end your turn so they see it. Do not call get_execution_result until the user replies; then call it once with held_execution_id. It waits up to 30 seconds (timeout, at most 30). If it is still held, show the user the review_url again and end your turn again. Do not re-send the call.

ExecuteAsync.description:
Execution queued — or held for human approval when a
`require-approval` permission rule matched (`status: held`; see
`HeldExecutionAcceptedResponse`). For a queued call, follow
`_links.self` to the control plane to poll the job and collect the
upstream response body once `status` is `completed`. The body is
delivered once and then evicted from the platform's pickup buffer.

Idempotent-Replayed.description:
Present and `true` when this `202` is a replay of a
previously-queued job under the same `Idempotency-Key`.
The `job_id` will match the original.

Jentic-Api-Vendor.description: API vendor hostname that was called.

Jentic-Operation.description: Name of the operation that was executed.

Preference-Applied.description: RFC 7240 — confirms which processing preference was applied.

schema.description:
Upstream response body, forwarded verbatim. Content type
varies by upstream API — may be JSON, XML, binary, or any
other media type. The `Content-Type` header on the response
reflects what the upstream returned.
schema.summary: Upstream response body forwarded by the Broker.
schema.title: UpstreamBody

ExecuteSync.description:
Synchronous success — upstream responded within the wait window.
The response body and status code are forwarded from the upstream
API.

Upstream response headers are forwarded as-is; broker-added
metadata is confined to the `Jentic-*` namespace.

Idempotent-Replayed.description:
Present and `true` when this response was replayed from a
stored `Idempotency-Key` rather than freshly executed.
Absent on first execution.

Jentic-Api-Vendor.description: API vendor hostname that was called.

Jentic-Operation.description: Name of the operation that was executed.

Jentic-Upstream-Status.description: HTTP status code returned by the upstream API.

Preference-Applied.description: RFC 7240 — confirms which processing preference was applied.

credential_binding_suspended.summary: The caller's binding for this API is suspended by its operator.

agent_directive.human_readable_instruction: Your operator has suspended your access to 'api.example.com/main'. Ask your operator whether they will resume it — only they can. Do not request a new connection for this API. Once they resume it, retry this call.

value.detail: The credential binding for this API is suspended
value.title: The credential binding for this API is suspended

value.detail: Insufficient scope: 'capabilities:execute' required
value.title: Forbidden

no_credential_binding.summary: Caller is not bound to any credential covering this API.

agent_directive.human_readable_instruction: You have no credential binding for 'api.example.com/main', but a credential already serves it. Ask your operator to bind this agent to that credential (in the dashboard, or via POST /agents/{agent_id}/credentials) — only a human can grant the binding. Once bound, retry this call.

value.detail: No credential binding for this API
value.title: No credential binding for this API

Forbidden.description:
Caller authenticated but not entitled to execute — most often a
token lacking the required `capabilities:execute` permission
(`type: insufficient_scope`, the RFC 6750 code), attempting to pin a `draft`
revision they don't own, using a credential they aren't bound to
(`no_credential_binding`), holding only a suspended binding for the
API (`credential_binding_suspended`), or being denied by a binding's
permission rules. Body is RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.

method_not_allowed.summary: The URL is registered only for other HTTP methods.

value.detail: Method not allowed; allowed: GET, PUT
value.title: Method not allowed; allowed: GET, PUT

MethodNotAllowed.description:
The upstream URL matches a registered API operation, but not for
the request's HTTP method (`method_not_allowed`). The broker answers
before dispatch, so the upstream never saw the call. The `Allow`
header and the `allowed_methods` member name the methods the URL
is registered for; resend with one of them. Body is RFC 9457
`application/problem+json`. A 405 the upstream itself returns is
mirrored with `error_origin: upstream` instead.

Allow.description: Comma-separated HTTP methods the upstream URL is registered for.

operation_not_found.summary: Upstream URL does not match any registered API operation.

value.detail: Operation not found — unregistered upstream URL.
value.title: Operation not found — unregistered upstream URL.

NotFound.description:
Upstream URL doesn't resolve to a registered API operation, or
the path component refers to a resource the upstream itself
doesn't recognise. Body is RFC 9457
`application/problem+json`.

payload_too_large.summary: Request body exceeded the per-Content-Type size cap.

value.detail: Request body exceeds the 10485760-byte cap.
value.title: Request body exceeds the 10485760-byte cap.

PayloadTooLarge.description:
Request body exceeded the broker's per-`Content-Type` size cap
(`max_request_bytes_by_type`, falling back to `max_request_bytes`).
The cap is resolved from the request `Content-Type` before the body is
read, so an over-cap upload fails fast. Body is RFC 9457
`application/problem+json`.

server_error.summary: Unhandled broker-side failure (details are logged, never echoed).

value.detail: An unexpected error occurred.
value.title: Internal Server Error

upstream_request_invalid.summary: The broker built an outbound request its HTTP client refused to send (e.g. an injected credential header carrying an illegal byte); fix the stored credential rather than retrying.

value.detail: Upstream transport error (LocalProtocolError)
value.title: Upstream transport error (LocalProtocolError)

ServerError.description:
Unexpected broker-side failure — a bug, a panic, or an outbound
request the broker itself built and could not send
(`upstream_request_invalid`, e.g. an injected credential header
with an illegal byte; fix the stored credential rather than
retrying). Should be rare; report with the `traceparent` header
for triage. Body is RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.

circuit_open.summary: Upstream circuit breaker is open; the broker is fast-failing.

value.detail: Upstream circuit open; the broker is fast-failing to let it recover.
value.title: Upstream circuit open; the broker is fast-failing to let it recover.

idempotency_unavailable.summary: The Idempotency-Key claim could not be recorded, so the request was not executed.

value.detail: The Idempotency-Key claim could not be recorded, so the request was not executed; retry after the indicated delay.
value.title: The Idempotency-Key claim could not be recorded, so the request was not executed; retry after the indicated delay.

server_at_capacity.summary: Instance shed the request at its in-flight admission cap.

value.detail: Server at capacity; retry shortly.
value.title: Server at capacity; retry shortly.

too_many_candidates.summary: The URL index returned more candidates than the broker can rank; nothing was dispatched.

value.detail: URL index returned too many candidates
value.title: URL index returned too many candidates

ServiceUnavailable.description:
Broker temporarily unable to serve traffic — startup,
shutdown, dependency outage, or a deliberate maintenance
window. Retry after the interval indicated by `Retry-After`.
Body is RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.

Retry-After.description:
Seconds to wait before retrying, per RFC 7231 §7.1.3.
May also be sent as an HTTP-date.

rate_limit_exceeded.summary: Caller exhausted their per-actor rate-limit window.

value.detail: Rate limit exceeded; slow down and retry after the indicated delay.
value.title: Rate limit exceeded; slow down and retry after the indicated delay.

TooManyRequests.description:
Caller exceeded their rate-limit window. Retry after the
interval indicated by `Retry-After`; the
`RateLimit-*` headers describe the current quota and
remaining budget per RFC 6648 / `draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers`.
Body is RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Total number of requests allowed in the current window.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in the current window.

Retry-After.description:
Seconds to wait before retrying, per RFC 7231 §7.1.3.
May also be sent as an HTTP-date.

invalid_token.summary: Token missing, unknown, revoked, or expired.

value.detail: Invalid or expired access token
value.title: Unauthorized

Unauthorized.description:
Authentication missing or invalid — the `Authorization: Bearer
<token>` credential is absent, malformed, expired, revoked, or
(for JWTs) signed by an issuer the Broker doesn't trust. Body is
RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.

invalid_revision_pin.summary: A Jentic-Revision value is not of the form vendor:name:version=<revision_id>.

value.detail: Malformed Jentic-Revision value: 'stripe:payments:2023-10-16=latest' (expected vendor:name:version=<revision_id>, with the revision_id from GET /apis/{vendor}/{name}/{version}/revisions)
value.title: Malformed Jentic-Revision value: 'stripe:payments:2023-10-16=latest' (expected vendor:name:version=<revision_id>, with the revision_id from GET /apis/{vendor}/{name}/{version}/revisions)

unknown_revision_pin.summary: Jentic-Revision pins a revision that does not exist.

value.detail: Unknown revision pin: stripe:payments:2023-10-16=3f2b8c1e-7d4a-4e9b-a6c5-1d2e3f4a5b6c
value.title: Unknown revision pin: stripe:payments:2023-10-16=3f2b8c1e-7d4a-4e9b-a6c5-1d2e3f4a5b6c

ValidationError.description:
Request well-formed but semantically invalid — e.g. unknown
revision pin, archived revision pin, or a request body that
fails the upstream operation's schema. Field-level details
live in the `errors[]` extension of the
`application/problem+json` body.

AgentDirective.description:
Machine-actionable recovery instruction embedded in a Broker
problem body. The fixed `strategy` vocabulary lets an agent
hard-code its recovery loop — e.g. on `wait` sleep
`parameters.retry_after_seconds`; on `modify_headers` add
`parameters.headers` and retry once; on `prompt_human` stop and
relay `human_readable_instruction` to the user.

examples.human_readable_instruction: Multiple bound credentials cover this API. Resend the same request with the Jentic-Credential-Id header set to one of the ids in parameters.candidates (Jentic-Credential-Name also works when names are unique).

human_readable_instruction.description: Plain-language instruction an agent can relay to a human or follow itself.
examples: Resend the same request with the Jentic-Credential-Id header set to one of the ids in parameters.candidates.

parameters.description:
Strategy-specific inputs (e.g. `headers` for `modify_headers`,
`retry_after_seconds` for `wait`, `intent_id` / `provisioning_url`
for `prompt_human`). Empty when the strategy needs none.

strategy.description: Recovery strategy the agent should apply.

AgentDirective.title: AgentDirective

AsyncQueuedResponse.description:
Returned as the `202` body on async executions. The Broker
does not expose a polling surface of its own; `_links.self`
is an absolute URL into the platform's control plane, where
the queued work surfaces as a `kind: execution` job. Poll
that URL for status, and follow its `_links.result` to
collect the upstream response body once `status` is
`completed`.

_links.description:
HAL-style link relations for the queued job. `self` always
points at the control-plane job record; the broker does
not expose its own polling surface.

self.description: Absolute URL of the control-plane job record. Poll this for status and result links.

_links.summary: HAL-style links pointing into the control-plane job record.
_links.title: AsyncQueuedResponseLinks

job_id.description: Unique identifier for the queued job. Matches the `job_id` reported by the control plane.
job_id.title: Job Id

status.description: Always `queued` on this body; a call held for approval answers `held` instead.
status.title: Status

AsyncQueuedResponse.summary: Handle returned when the Broker queues an upstream call for async execution.
AsyncQueuedResponse.title: AsyncQueuedResponse

allowed_methods.description:
The HTTP methods the upstream URL is registered for, on a
`method_not_allowed` 405. Mirrored in the `Allow` response
header.

candidates.description:
The caller's own credentials that matched ambiguously
(`ambiguous_credential_binding`, `ambiguous_credential`) or
that a credential-selection header failed to match
(`credential_id_not_found`, `credential_name_not_found`).
Pick one and resend with `Jentic-Credential-Id`.

error_origin.description:
Who generated the error response: `broker` (the Broker
itself — overloaded, misconfigured, rejecting the request
shape, or giving up on the call: an upstream timeout, a
dropped or refused upstream connection, the overall
deadline, a failed token refresh, an oversized upstream
response) or `upstream` (the external API answered with
this error and the Broker mirrored it). Mirrored in the
`Jentic-Error-Origin` response header. Absent on
authentication errors.

intent_id.description:
Correlation id for a `credential_not_provisioned` denial,
also carried in `agent_directive.parameters.intent_id`, so
the human hand-off can be tied back to this request.

BrokerProblem.description:
RFC 9457 Problem Details body for every Broker error. Extends the
shared Jentic `ProblemDetails` schema with the Broker's
agent-recovery members: `error_origin` says *who* failed, and
`agent_directive` (when present) is a machine-actionable recovery
instruction an agent can follow without parsing prose. `title`
repeats `detail` on Broker-originated errors.

examples.detail: No credential binding for this API
examples.title: No credential binding for this API

BrokerProblem.title: BrokerProblem

CredentialCandidate.description:
One of the caller's own credentials, distinguishable even when names
collide. Holds no secret material — `last4` is the last four
characters of the credential **id**.

created_at.description: When the credential was created, to tell same-named candidates apart.

id.description: Stable credential id; send it as `Jentic-Credential-Id` to pick this credential.

last4.description: Last four characters of the credential id, as a display hint.

CredentialCandidate.title: CredentialCandidate

HealthResponse.description:
Body returned by `GET /health` while the Broker process is
serving requests. Intentionally minimal — clients treat `200` +
`status: ok` as the green signal; the body is informational.

reason.description: Why the deployment is not entitled. Present only on the `not_entitled` body.
examples: Subscription for this deployment is not active.

status.description:
`ok` while the process is serving requests. A metered
marketplace deployment whose entitlement lapsed answers
`not_entitled` (still HTTP `200`, so orchestrators don't
restart it).

surface.description: Name of the surface reporting health; always `broker`. Absent on the `not_entitled` body.

version.description:
Running Jentic One release (the same version as `info.version`
in this spec). Absent on the `not_entitled` body.

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

HeldExecutionAcceptedResponse.description:
Returned as the `202` body when the call matches a permission rule
with `effect: require-approval`. The call has not run: it waits
until a reviewer (the agent's owner or an `org:admin`) approves or
denies it on `review_url`, or it expires. Follow `_links.self`
(`/executions/holds/{held_execution_id}`) to see where it stands;
once it has finished, `_links.result` returns the upstream response,
or the problem explaining why it never ran (denied, expired, or
refused at run time). To abandon the call, `POST` to
`_links.withdraw`. Never re-send the call: an identical call while
one is pending joins the same held execution.

result.description: The call's outcome, once it has finished.

self.description: The held execution — its decision and where the call stands.

withdraw.description:
`POST` here to withdraw the call before it is decided (only
the agent that made the call may). The call never runs.

agent_directive.description: What the calling agent should do next.

expires_at.description: When the call expires undecided and fails.

review_url.description: Review page; the reviewer signs in to decide. Carries no credential.

HeldExecutionAcceptedResponse.summary: Handle returned when a permission rule holds the call for human approval.
HeldExecutionAcceptedResponse.title: HeldExecutionAcceptedResponse

ReadinessResponse.description:
Body returned by `GET /ready`. `status: ready` (HTTP `200`) means the
instance is below the saturation threshold; `status: unready` (HTTP
`503`) means in-flight load is at/near the admission cap and the load
balancer should drain this instance. `saturation` is the current
in-flight count as a fraction of the configured cap.

reason.description: Why the instance is unready (present only on `unready`).

saturation.description:
In-flight requests as a fraction of the admission cap (`0`–`1`,
briefly above `1` at the cap edge). Omitted when the instance is
`draining`.

status.description:
`ready` while in-flight load is below the saturation threshold
(HTTP `200`); `unready` once it nears the admission cap (HTTP
`503`) and the load balancer should drain this instance.

ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

BearerAuth.description:
Credential authorizing a Broker call, sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The Broker accepts several
interchangeable credential formats, dispatched by prefix/shape:

- **Opaque access tokens** (`at_…`) — the *same* tokens the control
  plane issues from `POST /oauth/token`. A random string validated by
  server-side lookup (it is **not** a JWT and cannot be decoded by the
  client). Broker and control plane share one token store, so a token
  minted for the control plane authenticates here too.
- **API keys** — agent (`jak_…`) keys.
  May alternatively be sent in the `x-jentic-api-key` header. The
  `jntc_live_…` toolkit-key form is **retired** (theme-5): a value
  migrated before the toolkit tables were dropped still authenticates
  as its successor agent until the deprecation window closes (no
  earlier than 2026-12-01); rotate holders to that agent's `jak_` key.
  The `sak_…` service-account-key form is retired the same way
  (theme-8): a migrated value authenticates as its successor agent
  until its deprecation window closes.
- **Self-contained JWTs** — verified by signature (a dev HS256 shared
  secret or a configured trusted issuer with JWKS rotation). The Broker
  is identity-provider-agnostic: the IdP, federation strategy, and
  token-issuance flow are deployment concerns outside this spec.

Every protected operation requires the `capabilities:execute` permission,
whatever the credential format. Authorization beyond "may execute"
(agent-credential bindings, permission rules, revision pinning) is
enforced per-request and is not modelled here.

OAuth2.description:
OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE (`S256` only), run by the
control plane's authorization server. The resulting access token is
the same opaque `at_…` bearer token `BearerAuth` describes — the
Broker and control plane share one token store — sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Scopes are permission names; executing through the Broker requires
`capabilities:execute`. A scope only narrows a grant to a subset of
the actor's permissions, never widens it. Agents normally
authenticate with an agent API key or the control plane's
JWT-bearer grant instead — see `BearerAuth`.

info.description:
## Overview

The Broker is the platform's stateless data plane. Send it any
HTTP request with the upstream URL as the path; it injects the
caller's stored credentials, forwards method/headers/body as-is,
and returns the upstream response.

```
POST https://broker.your-instance.example/petstore.swagger.io/v2/pet
```

Secrets stay off agents and end-user devices, outbound traffic
has one auditable choke-point, and credentials rotate centrally
without redeploying callers. Sync responses return `200` with the
upstream body; long calls fall back to `202` with a polling link
into the control plane (see `Prefer` on `/{upstream_url}`).

Auth: every operation expects `Authorization: Bearer <token>` except
`GET /health`. Broker-added metadata is confined to the `Jentic-*`
header namespace — anything else on a response belongs to the
upstream.

Credential, agent-binding, and API-revision management live on the
[control plane](https://control.your-instance.example), not here.

## Path format

The request path **is** the upstream URL. The broker reconstructs the
full target from your path, adding `https://` when no scheme is present:

| You send | Broker proxies to |
|----------|-------------------|
| `GET /api.example.com/v1/users` | `https://api.example.com/v1/users` |
| `POST /petstore.swagger.io/v2/pet` | `https://petstore.swagger.io/v2/pet` |
| `GET /http://127.0.0.1:8080/get` | `http://127.0.0.1:8080/get` |
| `GET /https://api.example.com/v1/users` | `https://api.example.com/v1/users` |

For HTTPS upstream targets (the common case), omit the scheme — just use
`/{host}/{path}`. For plain HTTP targets (e.g. local development), include
the full `http://` scheme in the path so the broker doesn't upgrade to HTTPS.

Query strings pass through as-is: `/api.example.com/search?q=foo` works.

## Tracing and audit

Every brokered response carries W3C trace context (`traceparent`,
`tracestate`) and a `Jentic-*` header layer with the execution ID
(`exec_…`), the credential used (`Jentic-Credential-Id` /
`Jentic-Credential-Name`), and the upstream API reference
(`vendor:name:version`). OpenTelemetry clients pick this up
automatically; nothing else needs to parse `tracestate`.

To see what happened, ask the control plane:

- `GET /executions/{exec_id}` — full execution metadata (latency,
  status, pinned revisions, caller).
- `GET /executions` — list and filter recent executions.
- `GET /executions/{exec_id}/steps` — per-step trace for workflow
  executions.
- `GET /jobs/{job_id}` and `GET /jobs/{job_id}/result` — async
  job status and pickup of the upstream body.
- `GET /events` / `GET /events/stream` — audit event feed.

Request and response bodies are not persisted by default. Execution
metadata is retained for 30 days (configurable). Body capture is
explicit opt-in. Async response bodies live in a short-lived
pickup buffer collected via `/jobs/{id}/result`, not in the audit
store.
info.summary: Secure execution proxy for upstream APIs — credentials never leave the Broker.

get.description:
Unauthenticated liveness probe for the Broker service. Returns `200`
with a small JSON body while the process is serving requests,
reporting the surface name and the running Jentic One release.
Intended for load balancers, container orchestrators, and uptime
monitors — not for human or agent consumption beyond green/red
signalling. Use `/ready` for saturation-aware readiness.

notEntitled.summary: Metered marketplace deployment whose entitlement lapsed.

value.reason: Subscription for this deployment is not active.

200.description: Service is up and serving requests.

get.description:
Readiness probe distinct from liveness (`/health`). Returns `200`
while the instance can accept traffic and `503` once sustained
in-flight load nears the admission cap, so a load balancer drains
*this* instance before it begins shedding requests itself — without
the pod being restarted (liveness stays green). Intended for the
orchestrator `readinessProbe`, not for human or agent consumption.

200.description: Instance is ready to accept traffic.

503.description: Instance is saturated and should be drained.

delete.description:
Forward a `DELETE` to the upstream service. A request body is
permitted (RFC 7231 does not forbid one) and forwarded verbatim if
present, but most upstreams ignore it. Same response semantics as
`POST`.

delete_reason.summary: Optional body some upstreams accept on delete, forwarded as-is.

requestBody.description: Request body forwarded verbatim to the upstream service.

delete.summary: Execute a `DELETE` against an upstream API

/{upstream_url}.description:
Forward a request to the upstream API URL specified in the path. The
HTTP method you use on this endpoint is the method the broker sends to
the upstream service — every standard method (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`,
`PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`) is supported.

Request headers and body are forwarded as-is. The broker injects the
caller's stored credentials for the target API.

The path, query, and header parameters listed below apply to every
method. Per-method operations only differ in semantic intent and (for
methods that conventionally carry a body) in `requestBody` shape.

### Sync vs async

By default, the broker waits up to 30 seconds for the upstream
response. Control this with the `Prefer` header:

- `Prefer: wait=30` — wait up to 30 seconds, then fall back to async.
- `Prefer: respond-async` — always queue and return `202` immediately.

Async executions return a `202` with a polling link into the control plane.

### Error handling

Platform-level errors (auth failures, missing credentials) return an
RFC 9457 Problem Details (`application/problem+json`) body using the
shared `ProblemDetails` schema from
[jentic/api-problem-details](https://github.com/jentic/api-problem-details).
Field-level validation failures populate the `errors[]` extension.

### Idempotency

Optional `Idempotency-Key` request header (IETF
draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key). If present, the broker
records the key for 24 hours and replays the original response
for any subsequent request that reuses it — including `202`
handles, so retrying a queued async request returns the *same*
`job_id` instead of double-queueing the upstream call. Keys are
scoped per-caller and should be unique per logical operation
(UUIDv4 recommended, max 255 chars).

Replays are signalled with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` on the
response. If the same key is reused with a different request
body or upstream URL, the broker returns `409 Conflict`.

### Proxied upstream headers

On synchronous `200` responses, upstream API response headers are
forwarded as-is. Hop-by-hop headers (RFC 7230 §6.1) and the
broker's own trace/metadata headers are not proxied — every
broker-added header lives under the `Jentic-*` namespace, so
`Jentic-*` is unambiguously the broker's and anything else
belongs to the upstream.

### Security

The Broker validates every `upstream_url` against the set of
registered APIs before forwarding. Arbitrary URLs that do not
resolve to a known, registered API endpoint are rejected with
`404` — the Broker is **not** an open proxy. This allowlist
check is the spec's primary SSRF mitigation boundary:
credentials are never injected into requests targeting
unregistered hosts.

### Revision pinning

By default the Broker resolves the upstream URL against the
target API's `current_revision_id` (the `published` revision
registered on the control plane). To test a `draft` revision
with real credentials before promoting it, attach the
`Jentic-Revision` request header. The header is
multi-valued — repeat it (or comma-separate) once per API
you want to pin, with each value of the form
`vendor:name:version=<revision_id>` — the `revision_id` exactly
as the control plane's revision list returns it (the
`rev_<revision_id without hyphens>` label is equivalent).

The Broker forwards the pin into the control-plane
`POST /lookup/operation` call so URL → `operation_id`
resolution sees the requested spec. When the header is
absent or the URL doesn't match a pinned API, the Broker
resolves against `current_revision_id` as today.

Pinning a `draft` revision the caller doesn't have access to
returns `403`. Pinning an unknown or `archived` revision
returns `422` — `archived` revisions are deliberately not
pinnable from the hot path; resurrect them by re-promoting
instead. Pinning the same API to two different revisions in
one header returns `422 invalid_revision_pin`; repeating the
same revision (in either form) is allowed. The chosen
revisions are recorded on the resulting
`ExecutionRecord` (`pinned_revisions` field on the control
plane) so audit can answer "did this execution use a pinned
revision?" without parsing headers.

get.description:
Forward a `GET` to the upstream service. No request body. Typically
used for resource reads and listings; the upstream response is
returned verbatim on `200`, or queued and surfaced via `202` when
the wait window is exceeded or `Prefer: respond-async` is set.
get.summary: Execute a `GET` against an upstream API

head.description:
Forward a `HEAD` to the upstream service. No request body, no
response body — only headers. Useful for cheap existence /
last-modified checks. Async (`202`) is unusual for `HEAD` but
permitted for parity with the other methods.
head.summary: Execute a `HEAD` against an upstream API

options.description:
Forward an `OPTIONS` to the upstream service. Typically used for
CORS preflight discovery and capability probing. Same response
semantics as `GET`.
options.summary: Execute an `OPTIONS` against an upstream API

patch.description:
Forward a `PATCH` to the upstream service. Request body is forwarded
verbatim. Same response semantics as `POST`.

verbatim — the Broker does not inspect or transform it. The upstream
response is returned on `200`, or queued and surfaced via `202` when
the wait window is exceeded or `Prefer: respond-async` is set.
